items.title: SpaceX wants to launch Starship more than 450 times per year from South Texas
items.snippet: SpaceX has proposed increasing the number of allowed Starship launches from its Starbase site in South Texas from 25 per year to 456. The FAA is currently reviewing the request.

items.title: SpaceX Cargo Dragon delivers more than 6,000 pounds of supplies to the ISS
items.snippet: SpaceX's CRS-35 cargo Dragon rendezvoused and docked with the International Space Station today (Oct. 15) after a two-day chase, delivering more than 6,000 pounds of supplies to the orbtial laboratory's astronaut crew.

items.title: Planetary genealogy: Milky Way worlds belong to 1 of 2 'families,' scientists find

items.snippet: Artemis II mission specialist Christina Koch will become NASA's acting deputy chief engineer on Nov. 1. All four Artemis II crewmates have now stepped away from active spaceflight duties.

items.title: Climate warming can slow how tree roots feed soil microbes
items.snippet: A plant's roots do much of their work out of sight, pulling in water and nutrients and holding the plant in place. That makes it hard to see how plants respond when conditions underground change, and how a warming climate affects them. New Dartmouth-led studies look at the strategies plants use below the surface to adapt and survive.

items.title: About 2% of natural gas supplied to a Midwest city leaks into the atmosphere
items.snippet: Most natural gas leakage in Indianapolis likely originates from homes and other buildings, not exterior pipelines and large-scale distribution infrastructure that deliver the fossil fuel, according to Penn State researchers who assessed nearly a decade of data.

items.snippet: Structural metals used in engineering projects are expected to have both high strength and high ductility: the ability to withstand heavy loads and deform before failure. Achieving both of these properties at the same time, however, is challenging.

items.title: Automated essay assessment can grade writing more accurately across topics, study finds
items.snippet: An artificial intelligence (AI) model can score English essays with improved accuracy across different writing topics, according to work published in the International Journal of Continuing Engineering Education and Life-Long Learning. The tool could help schools assess student work more efficiently while reducing inconsistencies in grading.

items.title: Spiny dogfish blood contains a hormone long thought absent in sharks
items.snippet: Cortisol is a hormone that helps humans and many other animals regulate their energy use and respond to changing conditions. For a long time, sharks and rays were believed to rely on a different steroid hormone for these functions, without producing cortisol themselves. Now, a new study of North Pacific spiny dogfish, a species of small shark, challenges this view.

items.title: Maxwell's demon learns to turn concealed information into usable energy for microscopic systems
items.snippet: Since its introduction more than 150 years ago, the thought-provoking idea of Maxwell's demon has profoundly shaped our understanding of the relationship between information and energy. Maxwell's demon is an imagined microscopic gatekeeper that exploits information at the microscopic scale to produce macroscopic work.

items.title: Replanted landscapes can look restored while soil fungi still lag behind
items.snippet: With up to 75% of the world's soils degraded, restoration projects try to reestablish functional and biodiverse environments to secure adequate food production, biodiversity, climate regulation and human well-being.

items.title: Finding their sense of direction: Cell movement helps tissues establish polarity
items.snippet: From the hairs on our arms to the microscopic sensory structures of the inner ear, many tissues in the body are built with a clear sense of direction. To build these structures throughout development, individual cells must establish which way they are facing—and coordinate that orientation with cells around them.
